title.narrative: Output 4.2. Strengthened capacity of enterprises and their support systems to enhance productivity and sustainability

description.narrative: On 28 July 2022, the Gambia Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GCCI), launched the first ever televised business plan competition in The Gambia. The aim of this competition, which has consolidated the efforts made by the GCCI over the years in promoting entrepreneurship, business management and access to finance, was to encourage young potential entrepreneurs to create sustainable enterprises both in urban and rural areas, as well as to promote innovation and merit. The competition has been named "Keur Jula Challenge" to resonate with local audiences and competitors. The business plan competition brought together 450 candidates (61% of whom were women) from all regions of The Gambia. 252 shortlisted candidates (53% of whom were women) were auditioned over the period November - December 2022. 19 candidates (68% of whom were women) were awarded financial and non-financial prizes. In collaboration with the Italian government, through the PROMEFI project, the ILO supported the GCCI in the conceptualisation and organisation of the "Keur Jula Challenge" business plan competition. Fifteen (15) business advisers (out of which 7 women) from the GCCI were trained in the business plan competition methodology and 167 candidates (53% of whom were women) attended the Start Your Business (SYB) training course between August 2022 and February 2023. The participants in the semi-finals and final were also supported through specific coaching services and they participated in a ad-hoc training on pitching. A guide on access to social security was launched in April and delivered in June 2022. This was followed by the training of 10 GCCI business advisers to deliver awareness-raising sessions on the subject. Similarly, 20 entrepreneurs participated in an information session on the importance of social protection for their workers and their companies.

description.narrative: The Gambian government, through the Ministry of Trade, Industry, Regional Integration and Employment (MOTIE), the social partners and representative of the informal economy have carried out a diagnostic of informal enterprises and their workers. The document was validated on 21st September 2022. This diagnostic has enabled a better understanding of the informal sector, such as its extent and diversity, as well as the causes and consequences of informality among informal enterprises and their workers. The diagnostic served as a major reference document for the development of the National strategy for the formalization of the informal economy in The Gambia, which is due to be validated on 23rd September 2023. In May - June 2022 the ILO has organised and rolled out a distance-leaning course on enterprise formalisation for the Gambian tripartite constituents and other relevant stakeholders. The objective of the training programme was to familiarize constituents and other stakeholders with the major challenges and drivers of informality in The Gambia in general and in informal MSMEs (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) in particular. It also explored ways to leverage the potential of actors in the informal sector for decent work and inclusive growth through formalization, based on the ILO approach on enterprise formalization and good practices in this field. The training aimed to build institutional and individual capacities to put in place effective strategies and initiatives aimed at formalizing micro and small enterprises as well as the workers they employ. Furthermore, the ILO the tripartite constituents with the technical expertise in carrying out the diagnostic study on the informal enterprises and their workers, as well as to organise and carry out country-wide consultations to inform the development of the National strategy for the formalization of the informal economy in The Gambia. A specific technical assistance was provided to align the National strategy to the national priorities and the ILO Recommendation 204.
